facts.raw_span: A 30-year-old man
asymptomatic, calcified mass on the right anterior maxilla
had been present for 18 months
mucosal fenestration through which a hard, mineralized structure approximately 1 cm in diameter was visible
a discrete radiopaque lesion
periapical radiograph of the upper right premolar area
initial diagnostic hypothesis was maxillary exostosis
incisional biopsy was performed
a fragment of the lesion, which was submitted for histopathological analysis

concepts.why: The presence of a calcified mass on the right anterior maxilla and a mucosal fenestration with a hard, mineralized structure is consistent with maxillary exostosis.
The discrete radiopaque lesion and the incisional biopsy suggest an odontogenic tumor, which is a type of bone lesion.
The hard, mineralized structure and the mucosal fenestration are consistent with a periosteal osteoma, a type of bone lesion.
The discrete radiopaque lesion and the incisional biopsy suggest a compound odontoma, which is a type of bone lesion.
The calcified mass and the mucosal fenestration are consistent with a fibro-osseous lesion, which is a type of bone lesion.
The presence of a hard, mineralized structure is consistent with a mandibular torus, although the location is atypical.
The discrete radiopaque lesion and the incisional biopsy suggest an osteoma, which is a type of bone lesion.
The calcified mass and the mucosal fenestration are consistent with a cemento-ossifying fibroma, which is a type of bone lesion.
